title: Issue 4: conditional job writes and durable persistence

requirements.expectation: Every service_requests writer is inventoried, including server code, API routes, SQL functions, scheduled operations, and remaining clients.
requirements.verification: Search all direct insert/update/upsert/delete operations and database functions; map each to its version/concurrency behavior.
evidence: Direct writers were reviewed in job-store, pairing, negotiation, payment confirmation, payout, admin, care, and job API paths; complete independent inventory sign-off remains pending
Express assignment/cancellation uses explicit pending/draft-state predicates; Express remains a separate financial lifecycle

requirements.expectation: Persisted jobs carry a monotonic version that is selected, mapped, and advanced by every successful mutation.
requirements.verification: Review schema migration, row mapping, projections, RPCs, fixtures, and every writer; confirm old rows receive a safe initial value.
evidence: supabase/migrations/20261007_079_job_version_cas.sql adds the defaulted version column and update trigger
JobRecord and row mapping include jobVersion; LEAN_JOB_COLUMNS selects it

requirements.expectation: Every job write is conditional on the version or an equally strong expected-state predicate, and stale writers cannot overwrite a newer job.
requirements.verification: Review every writer and race/conflict evidence, including Issue 3 timeout and pairing SQL paths.
evidence: job-store/cache.ts compares job_version for full-patch persistence; pairing and negotiation paths compare the loaded version
Direct status writers in API, care, admin, and payout paths use job_version or a narrow expected-state predicate; complete independent call-site review remains pending

requirements.expectation: Persistence does not retry a failed full patch with smaller patches that silently omit requested fields.
requirements.verification: Inspect persistence helper and failure paths; verify schema/database errors fail the operation visibly.
evidence: job-store/cache.ts removes reduced-patch retries and does not issue a second unconditional write
job-store/create.ts fails instead of retrying an insert after dropping motorist_vehicle

requirements.expectation: Process memory is only a disposable cache and never authorizes a job read or critical write when durable storage is unavailable.
requirements.verification: Inspect DB read failures, missing DB configuration, create/update paths, and cache invalidation or refresh behavior.
evidence: Process-local job Map and all job-store memory fallback reads/writes were removed; database errors now fail job reads and writes

requirements.expectation: Version conflicts are distinguishable from storage failures, and each workflow handles conflicts safely without replaying unsafe side effects.
requirements.verification: Trace callers and verify conflict recovery, reload, or user-facing retry behavior is appropriate to the operation.
evidence: JobWriteConflictError returns HTTP 409 and JobPersistenceUnavailableError returns HTTP 503 on the main job endpoints
persistIfUnchanged returns null only for a no-row conflict and propagates storage errors

requirements.expectation: Job state-machine, assignment, payment, fee, refund, and deadline rules retain their current behavior.
requirements.verification: Review diff against protected-flow rules and existing behavior evidence; identify any intentional rule change separately.
evidence: No fee formulas or timer constants changed; state-machine and protected pricing files are untouched

requirements.expectation: The implementation does not claim cross-table atomicity for job, escrow, callout, or event writes unless a transaction/RPC provides it.
requirements.verification: Inspect side-effect ordering and documentation; carry remaining aggregate gaps to Issue 5.
evidence: Issue 5 transaction boundary remains explicitly separate; event and multi-table effects can still partially complete

requirements.expectation: The version migration applies safely to existing rows and can be deployed without silently leaving writers outside the concurrency contract.
requirements.verification: Apply migration to an isolated database, verify existing-row initialization and all relevant SQL functions, then record hosted rollout separately.
evidence: Migration is idempotent and transaction-wrapped; hosted and isolated database application have not been verified

requirements.expectation: Relevant checks and failure/concurrency scenarios pass for the exact reviewed commit.
requirements.verification: Record commands, outcomes, commit SHA, and evidence for stale writes, failed persistence, and database outage behavior.
evidence: npm run lint passed with 0 errors and 159 warnings
npm test -- --reporter=dot passed: 101 files, 1,209 tests; focused test covers scheduled-dispatch CAS loss
Hosted migration and runtime evidence are pending

implementationNotes: Implementation notes and evidence are in docs/review-guides/issue-4-job-persistence.md.
implementationState: Implementation and automated checks complete in working tree; formal code review and migration verification pending

independentReview.scope: To be performed against the implementation commit
